hunks.baseline: The boy—or rather, the “he” bearing the name Mungyeong—looked down at the ground below his feet.
hunks.sol: The boy—no, the man called Mungyeong—looked down at those below.

hunks.baseline: Countless eyes gazed up at him in disbelief. Among them was a familiar face.
hunks.sol: Countless eyes stared up at him in disbelief. Among them was a familiar face.

hunks.baseline: They had only met once, a long time ago, but recognizing him was not difficult.
hunks.sol: They had met only once, long ago, but it was not difficult to recognize him.

hunks.baseline: The greatest assassin under heaven. A man who had inspired awe in countless martial artists beyond condemnation and contempt had vanished without a trace one day and never shown himself again.
hunks.sol: The greatest assassin under heaven. He had inspired not merely condemnation and contempt in countless martial artists, but awe. Then one day, he had vanished without a trace, never to appear again.

hunks.baseline: At least, not until a moment ago.
hunks.sol: At least, not until moments ago.

hunks.baseline: “A lot has happened. So very much. Isn’t that right?”
hunks.sol: “A great deal has happened. A great deal indeed. Wouldn’t you agree?”

hunks.baseline: The question was directed at an old man. He gazed at the Divine Physician—or rather, Dong Feng—with indescribable eyes before opening his lips.
hunks.sol: The question was directed at an old man. The man called Mungyeong gazed at the Divine Physician—or rather, Dong Feng—with an indescribable look before speaking.

hunks.baseline: “What a relief. I wasn’t too late.”
hunks.sol: “Thank goodness. I wasn’t too late.”

hunks.baseline: Everyone shuddered at the unfathomable heights of martial arts displayed before their eyes. The old physician quietly shook his head.
hunks.sol: A shudder ran through everyone at the unfathomable realm of martial arts displayed before them. The old physician quietly shook his head.

hunks.baseline: A note of regret followed.
hunks.sol: His next words carried a note of regret.

hunks.baseline: “To turn back the years that have passed.”
hunks.sol: “Too late to turn back the years that have passed.”

hunks.baseline: “What can be done? Once water has spilled, gathering it back is no easy task.”
hunks.sol: “What can be done? Once water is spilled, it is not easily gathered again.”

hunks.baseline: At his Disciple’s words, he raised his head and looked toward the sky.
hunks.sol: At his Disciple’s words, he raised his head toward the sky.

hunks.baseline: The rain that had seemed as if it would pour forever and the black clouds that had hidden the sunlight were gone. An azure heaven stretched across the sky.
hunks.sol: The rain that had seemed as though it would fall forever was gone, as were the dark clouds that had blotted out the sun. All that remained was the vast azure heaven.

hunks.baseline: He posed the question to someone who might be looking down at the lower realm from above.
hunks.sol: He posed the question to someone who might be looking down upon the mortal realm from above.
But no answer came.

hunks.baseline: But no answer came. Just as it never had.
hunks.sol: Just as it never had.

hunks.baseline: *What a damnable thing this is.*
hunks.sol: *What a damned thing this is.*

hunks.baseline: The life he had lived as an assassin after being raised as one. His inborn karma had made him an assassin, so he killed people—but he had been born a human being, and he hated killing.
hunks.sol: He had been raised as an assassin and lived as one. His inborn karma was that of an assassin, so he killed—but he had been born human, and he hated killing.

hunks.baseline: That was why, at the end of the great war that had stained the continent with blood, the old assassin buried his weapons and began living as a physician.
hunks.sol: That was why, near the end of the great war that had stained the continent with blood, the aging assassin had buried his weapons and chosen to live as a physician.

hunks.baseline: Had it truly come to this in the end?
hunks.sol: Had it come to this after all?

hunks.baseline: With a faint murmur, he opened his eyes.
hunks.sol: With a quiet murmur, he opened his eyes.

hunks.baseline: A boy’s hands, white and soft.
hunks.sol: A boy’s hands, pale and soft.

hunks.baseline: The Returned to Youth he had undergone several years ago had changed his flesh, but it could not erase the scent of blood ingrained in his hands.
hunks.sol: Returned to Youth had transformed his flesh several years ago, but even that could not erase the scent of blood steeped into his hands.

hunks.baseline: “I lived for more than forty years as a physician. I wanted to die as one.”
hunks.sol: “I lived as a physician for more than forty years. I wished to die as one.”

hunks.baseline: His voice, carrying immense internal energy, thundered into everyone’s ears. The black-clad men staggered as if their very spirits had been shaken.
hunks.sol: His voice, laden with immense internal energy, struck their ears like thunder. The black-clad men staggered as though the sound had shaken their very souls.

hunks.baseline: “And yet, why have you come here?”
hunks.sol: “And yet, why did you come here?”

hunks.baseline: Killing intent that made every hair on the body stand on end radiated from him. The deputy captain, who had frozen while staring at the being in the sky, spoke in a trembling voice.
hunks.sol: His killing intent made every hair stand on end. The deputy captain, frozen as he stared at the figure in the sky, spoke in a trembling voice.

hunks.baseline: “E-Even if you truly are the Slaughter Saint, this is not your concern.”
hunks.sol: “E-Even if you truly are the Slaughter Saint, this is no concern of yours.”

hunks.baseline: “Not my concern?”
hunks.sol: “No concern of mine?”

hunks.baseline: He muttered the words in a low voice before throwing down the travel bag he had been holding.
hunks.sol: He repeated the words in a low voice, then tossed down the travel bag in his hand.

hunks.baseline: Something bounced out of the bag when it struck the ground and landed at the deputy captain’s feet.
hunks.sol: Something bounced out of the bag as it struck the ground and rolled to the deputy captain’s feet.

hunks.baseline: They were the severed heads of two men. Though they belonged to different people, their wide eyes and twisted expressions looked almost exactly alike.
hunks.sol: They were the severed heads of two men. Though they belonged to different people, their bulging eyes and twisted expressions looked almost identical.

hunks.baseline: As if they were twins born on the same day.
hunks.sol: Like twins born at the same hour on the same day.

hunks.baseline: The deputy captain stared in horror at the First Fiend’s severed head. Slowly, the man opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: As the deputy captain stared in horror at First Fiend’s severed head, the Slaughter Saint slowly spoke.

hunks.baseline: “I’ll ask you one thing. Was the one in Qingcheng the second or the third of the Qilian Three Fiends?”
hunks.sol: “One question. Was the one at Qingcheng the second or third of the Qilian Three Fiends?”

hunks.baseline: Why there had been no word from the Qingcheng Sect. And where his brothers, who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal, were.
hunks.sol: Why no word had come from the Qingcheng Sect—and where the brothers who had failed to return after seeing the emergency signal had gone.

hunks.baseline: In the end, only one path remained.
With a flash of insight, he shouted with internal energy behind his voice.
hunks.sol: There was only one course left to him. The realization struck like lightning, and he unleashed a shout imbued with internal energy.

hunks.baseline: The deputy captain could not finish his shout.
hunks.sol: The deputy captain’s shout was cut short.

hunks.baseline: Along with the wind brushing his neck, a figure stood behind him.
hunks.sol: A breeze brushed his neck, and suddenly someone was standing behind him.

hunks.baseline: *Is this really… a human movement?*
hunks.sol: *Can this truly be… the movement of a human being?*

hunks.baseline: That was the last question to pass through his mind.
hunks.sol: That was the last question to cross his mind.

hunks.baseline: He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, in all history.
hunks.sol: He had failed to recognize the Ghost Illusory Slaughter Step performed by the greatest assassin under heaven—or rather, the greatest assassin in all history.

hunks.baseline: A fountain of blood erupted from the severed neck. As a figure brushed past his collapsing body and took another step, wind carrying the scent of blood swept through the air.
hunks.sol: Blood erupted from the severed neck in a fountain. A figure brushed past the collapsing body and took another step, stirring a wind heavy with the scent of blood.

hunks.baseline: The black-clad men who had watched their superior die with vacant expressions saw their heads rise into the air.
hunks.sol: The heads of the black-clad men who had watched their superior die in a daze flew into the air.

hunks.baseline: Before the streams of blood could even touch the ground, something pale and ghostlike passed through them.
hunks.sol: Before the streams of blood could reach the ground, something pale and ghostlike swept through them.

hunks.baseline: “It was the life I wanted so badly.”
hunks.sol: “It was the life I wanted so desperately.”

hunks.baseline: Muttering in a low voice, he stretched out both hands. Thin, elongated threads flowed from his ten fingers.
hunks.sol: Murmuring under his breath, he extended both hands. Long, slender threads streamed from his ten fingers.

hunks.baseline: Threads of Force—beautiful and destructive.
hunks.sol: Beautiful and destructive threads of Sword Force.

hunks.baseline: When his ten curved fingers slashed downward through the air, Force tore through space.
hunks.sol: His ten curved fingers raked downward through the air, and Sword Force tore through space.

hunks.baseline: Everything that stood in its way was cut apart and split open. Shattered armor and weapons, limbs and heads, flew in every direction.
hunks.sol: Everything in its path was slashed apart. Shattered armor and weapons, severed limbs and heads—all flew in every direction.

hunks.baseline: In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person was free to move.
hunks.sol: In a world brought to a standstill by blood and death, only one person moved freely.

hunks.baseline: “Did you wake me?”
hunks.sol: “…wake me?”

hunks.baseline: Consumed by sorrow and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy or the physician who had passed the two-character name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.
hunks.sol: Consumed by grief and fury, he was no longer the cheerful boy, nor was he the physician who had passed the name Divine Physician down to his Disciple.

hunks.baseline: He had returned to the person he had been before earning the name Divine Physician, before meeting the young carpenter who had fallen into grief after losing his wife and children to an epidemic, and before burying his weapons and leaving the Murim.
hunks.sol: He had become the man he had been before earning the name Divine Physician. Before meeting the young carpenter who had fallen into despair after losing his wife and children to an epidemic. Before burying his weapons and leaving Murim behind.

hunks.baseline: Someone shouted the words like a scream.
hunks.sol: Someone screamed the name.

hunks.baseline: With eyes sunk deeper than an abyss, he flung out both arms. The wind, which had already become a storm, swallowed more than a hundred black-clad men.
hunks.sol: His eyes had sunk deeper than the abyss. He flung out both arms, and the wind—now a raging storm—swallowed more than a hundred black-clad men.

hunks.baseline: There was a high hill east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: A high hill stood east of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: From that hill, the entire Tang Clan grounds could be seen at a glance. A small watchtower had once stood there, along with martial artists who took turns standing guard.
hunks.sol: From there, one could see the entire Tang Clan estate at a glance. A small watchtower stood atop it, and martial artists had once taken turns standing guard.

hunks.baseline: Drops of blood fell from the watchtower and dampened the grass. Some slid down the hill and touched someone’s hand.
hunks.sol: Drops of blood fell from the watchtower and darkened the grass. Some rolled down the slope until they touched a hand.

hunks.baseline: The hand was covered in deep wrinkles, and the nails had taken on a green hue from years of practicing poison arts.
hunks.sol: Its back was deeply wrinkled, and its nails had turned green from long years spent practicing poison arts.

hunks.baseline: The owner of that hand was Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.
hunks.sol: The hand belonged to Tang Sadok, the current Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan—the Myriad-Poison Asura.

hunks.baseline: Blood spattered between his parched lips. His eyes, usually cold and forceful, looked ready to go out at any moment.
hunks.sol: Blood sprayed from between his parched lips. His eyes, usually cold and forceful, looked ready to go out at any moment.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok murmured in a faint voice.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok murmured faintly.

hunks.baseline: Everything was rushing toward its end. His life. The glorious history of the Sichuan Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: Everything was racing toward its end. His life. The glorious history of the Sichuan Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: “The family we built over hundreds of years… is collapsing in a single day.”
hunks.sol: “Our family, built over centuries… brought down in a single day.”

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok’s lament was hollow. He no longer had the strength even to feel anger or sorrow.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok’s lament rang hollow. He no longer possessed the strength even to feel anger or sorrow.

hunks.baseline: With his limbs crushed and his internal injuries severe, the only thing permitted to the old Family Head was to lean against an unnamed tree and watch his clan perish.
hunks.sol: His limbs crushed and his internal injuries severe, all the old Family Head could do was lean against an unknown tree and watch his clan perish.

hunks.baseline: The middle-aged man, the Western Heaven Demon Lord, had not kept his promise. As far as he was concerned, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been decided from the very beginning.
hunks.sol: The Western Heaven Demon Lord had not kept his promise. To him, the destruction of the Sichuan Tang Clan had been a foregone conclusion from the very beginning.

hunks.baseline: “Urgh. Blergh!”
hunks.sol: “Urgh… Blergh!”

hunks.baseline: The resentment blazing up like a wildfire worsened his internal injuries. Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood and gasped for breath.
hunks.sol: The rage flaring within him like wildfire worsened his internal injuries. Tang Sadok vomited nearly half a gallon of blood, then gasped for breath.

hunks.baseline: He was apologizing to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan, to the blameless members of his household who had lost their lives under an unworthy Family Head, and to Jin Taekyung and the others, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.
hunks.sol: It was an apology to the ancestors of the Sichuan Tang Clan. To the innocent members of his household who had lost their lives because they had been saddled with an unworthy Family Head. And to Jin Taekyung and his companions, who had likely already met gruesome deaths at the hands of the Western Heaven Demon Lord.

hunks.baseline: Of course, not one of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.
hunks.sol: Of course, none of them could hear Tang Sadok’s voice.

hunks.baseline: *If we meet in the afterlife, I’ll apologize to you myself.*
hunks.sol: *If we meet in the afterlife, I will apologize to you myself.*

hunks.baseline: It was then, as Tang Sadok murmured inwardly—
hunks.sol: Just as Tang Sadok murmured those words inwardly—

hunks.baseline: Sssshhk.
hunks.sol: Rustle.

hunks.baseline: The bushes stirred, and he felt something approaching.
hunks.sol: The bushes stirred, and he sensed something approaching.

hunks.baseline: Only when it reached the very tip of his nose did Tang Sadok realize who possessed that strange presence.
hunks.sol: Only when the strange presence had drawn right up to him did Tang Sadok realize who it belonged to.

hunks.baseline: A triangular head with horns and a flicking tongue. A snake with a pure-white body burrowed into Tang Sadok’s embrace.
hunks.sol: A flicking tongue. A horned, triangular head. A pure-white snake burrowed into Tang Sadok’s arms.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok laughed weakly, both happy and hollow.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok slumped back with a laugh, both overjoyed and heartsick.

hunks.baseline: The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as if answering its master. Its cold tongue licked the beard matted with blood.
hunks.sol: The Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake, Mimi, hissed as though answering her master. Her cold tongue licked his beard, which was matted with blood.

hunks.baseline: “Clever creature. How did you find your way all the way here?”
hunks.sol: “Clever creature. How did you find me all the way out here?”

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok looked at his pet snake with blurred eyes.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok gazed at his pet snake through clouded eyes.

hunks.baseline: He had let Mimi loose because he was worried the snake might be injured in the melee. He had never thought they would meet again like this.
hunks.sol: He had set her loose out of fear that she might be hurt in the chaotic battle. He had never expected them to meet again like this.

hunks.baseline: And he had never imagined that their final farewell would be like this, either.
hunks.sol: Nor had he imagined their final farewell would happen this way.

hunks.baseline: A tremendous roar shook the hill. The earth rose, and the branches of the trees trembled.
hunks.sol: A tremendous roar sent tremors all the way up the hill. The ground heaved, and the trees shook their branches.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source of the roar, but with his vision already clouded, he could not tell what was happening.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok raised his head and tried to find the source, but his failing eyesight could no longer make out what was happening.

hunks.baseline: He could only infer one thing.
hunks.sol: He could infer only one thing.

hunks.baseline: The roar was on an entirely different level from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.
hunks.sol: It was a roar on an entirely different scale from Heaven-Shaking Thunder.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok slowly closed and opened his eyes before speaking.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok slowly closed his eyes, then opened them again.

hunks.baseline: The snake’s triangular snout tilted to one side.
hunks.sol: The triangular head tilted to one side.

hunks.baseline: “This old man and the Tang Clan have little time left. If you stay here, you will be caught up in it as well.”
hunks.sol: “This old man has little time left. Neither does the Tang Clan. If you stay here, you will be caught up in this calamity as well.”

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Even if the Western Heaven Demon Lord did not come, someone would certainly come to confirm whether he was alive or dead.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok was the Family Head of the Sichuan Tang Clan. Even if the Western Heaven Demon Lord did not come himself, someone would certainly come to confirm whether he was alive or dead.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok could easily imagine what those vicious men would do if they saw the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake guarding its master’s side.
hunks.sol: He could easily imagine what the murderers would do if they found the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake guarding her master’s side.

hunks.baseline: He wanted to shout, but the voice he forced out was so thin it seemed ready to break apart.
hunks.sol: He wanted to roar the words, but the voice he wrung out was so thin it seemed ready to snap.

hunks.baseline: Yet the spirit creature that had spent so many years beside Tang Sadok understood the final wish of the man who had been both its master and its friend.
hunks.sol: Yet the spiritual creature that had spent so many years beside him understood the final wish of the man who had been both her master and her friend.

hunks.baseline: Damp drops fell onto Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand.
hunks.sol: Warm droplets fell onto the back of Tang Sadok’s wrinkled hand.

hunks.baseline: Leaving behind a few tears, Mimi slithered away and disappeared, the snake’s white body gliding across the ground.
hunks.sol: Leaving behind a few tears, Mimi slithered away, her white body gliding across the ground.

hunks.baseline: As Mimi’s presence faded into the distance, a bitter smile briefly formed at the corner of Tang Sadok’s mouth.
hunks.sol: As her presence receded into the distance, a bitter smile briefly touched Tang Sadok’s lips.

hunks.baseline: “Yes. Go carefully.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Go safely.”

hunks.baseline: In his youth, he had roamed the battlefields. After the war ended, he had devoted his entire life to helping his father, the Poison King, rebuild the Sichuan Tang Clan.
hunks.sol: In his youth, he had roamed the battlefields. After the war, he had devoted his life to helping his father, the Poison King, rebuild the Sichuan Tang Clan.

hunks.baseline: He had always been required to remain cold-headed and thorough. He had no friend with whom he could share his heart, no lover, and no child born of his blood.
hunks.sol: He had always been expected to remain cold and meticulous. He had no friend with whom he could share his heart, no lover, and no child of his own blood.

hunks.baseline: If not for the spirit creature that had remained at his side for so long, he would never have been able to endure his loneliness.
hunks.sol: Had that spiritual creature not remained by his side all those years, he could never have endured the loneliness.

hunks.baseline: “From today onward, your name is Mimi. Tang Mimi.”
hunks.sol: *From today onward, your name is Mimi. Tang Mimi.*

hunks.baseline: The blood flowing through Mimi was different. Even the snake’s species was different. But Tang Mimi was a member of the Sichuan Tang Clan, recognized as such by its Family Head.
hunks.sol: They shared neither blood nor even species, but Tang Mimi was a member of the Sichuan Tang Clan, recognized as such by its Family Head.

hunks.baseline: *I’ve lost everyone, and I’m sending only you away alive. Hahaha.*
hunks.sol: *I have lost everyone, and you alone are the one I send away alive. Hahaha.*

hunks.baseline: Through his fading senses, the roar and someone’s screams echoed faintly from below the hill.
hunks.sol: Through his fading senses, he heard distant roars and screams rising from below the hill.

hunks.baseline: It must have been the final struggle of those resisting the destruction of the clan.
hunks.sol: It must have been the final struggle of those fighting to stave off the clan’s destruction.

hunks.baseline: *This old man is here, too. I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!*
hunks.sol: *This old man is still here! I, Tang Sadok, Family Head of the great Sichuan Tang Clan, am here! Come to me!*

hunks.baseline: The cry, as if he were coughing up blood, only hovered at the tip of his tongue.
hunks.sol: The cry, as though wrenched from his throat with blood, never made it past the tip of his tongue.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok slowly felt the strength drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids tilted downward, little by little, ever so slowly.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok felt the strength slowly drain from his entire body. His heavy eyelids sank lower, little by little.

hunks.baseline: What would happen if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?
hunks.sol: What if he simply closed his eyes and fell into a deep sleep?

hunks.baseline: If he took a short nap and awoke in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall, perhaps he would be able to see the familiar faces of his family.
hunks.sol: Perhaps, after a brief nap, he would awaken in the grand armchair in the Family Head’s Hall and find the familiar faces of his household waiting for him.

hunks.baseline: How wonderful would it be if everything that had happened up to now—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream?[^1]
hunks.sol: How wonderful it would be if everything that had happened—including his father’s death—were nothing more than a Butterfly Dream.[^1]

hunks.baseline: *Yes. If only that were true.*
hunks.sol: *Yes. If only it were.*

hunks.baseline: Slowly. His trembling eyelids finally closed tight.
hunks.sol: His trembling eyelids slowly sank shut.

hunks.baseline: No, it was the moment before they closed.
hunks.sol: No—they were just about to close.

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok involuntarily opened his eyes wide.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok’s eyes flew open.

hunks.baseline: In his suddenly brightened field of vision, he saw a young man running toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting forward like an arrow.
hunks.sol: His vision suddenly cleared, revealing a young man racing toward him and Mimi’s white body shooting through the air like an arrow.

hunks.baseline: “Wow! Wild Grandpa Tang spotted!”
hunks.sol: “Wow! A wild Grandpa Tang appeared!”

hunks.baseline: At the sight of Cheongpung grinning brightly with blood all over his face, Tang Sadok blinked.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok blinked at Cheongpung, who was grinning brightly despite the blood covering his face.

hunks.baseline: “What… what is going on? How did you…?”
hunks.sol: “What… What is going on? How did you…?”

hunks.baseline: If Tang Sadok had possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed him out.
hunks.sol: Had Tang Sadok possessed even a shred of strength, he would have cursed them both out.

hunks.baseline: Forgetting that he had been half dead a moment ago, Tang Sadok stared blankly at the one man and one snake before him. With difficulty, he opened his mouth.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok forgot that he had been half dead only moments ago and stared blankly at the man and snake before him. At last, he managed to speak.

hunks.baseline: “Our family—what happened to our family?”
hunks.sol: “Our family… What happened to our family?”

hunks.baseline: “Oh. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men, not the Tang Clan.”
hunks.sol: “Oh. Not the Tang Clan. I meant Dark Heaven’s black-clad men.”

hunks.baseline: Just as Tang Sadok was unable to continue speaking from shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed Tang Sadok’s Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day caressed his body.
hunks.sol: As Tang Sadok choked on shock and fury, Cheongpung pressed a finger to his Mingmen acupoint. Warmth like a spring day seeped into his body.

hunks.baseline: *This bastard is going to keep doing this to the end…*
hunks.sol: *This bastard is going to keep this up until the very end…*

hunks.baseline: Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the sleep washing over him.
hunks.sol: Tang Sadok wanted to ask what had happened, but this time he could not resist the drowsiness washing over him.

hunks.baseline: Just before his eyelids closed, a soft voice like a spring breeze brushed against his ears.
hunks.sol: Just before his eyelids closed, a voice as gentle as a spring breeze reached his ears.

hunks.baseline: It was the voice announcing the end of a day that had been longer and darker than any other.
hunks.sol: It was the voice that announced the end of a day longer and darker than any other.

hunks.baseline: [^1]: The Butterfly Dream is an allusion to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi’s dream that he was a butterfly, leaving him uncertain afterward whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.
hunks.sol: [^1]: The Butterfly Dream alludes to the ancient Chinese philosopher Zhuangzi’s dream that he was a butterfly, after which he wondered whether he was a man who had dreamed of being a butterfly or a butterfly dreaming of being a man.
